t: The amendments made by this Act shall take effect on January 1, 1972, except that the amendments made by sections 2(35) and 2(36) of this Act shall take effect only with respect to benefit years that begin on or after January 2, 1972.

fable.w: This section is purely an effective-date provision specifying when amendments take effect. It involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government; there is no tempting participatory reading.

opus.w: This is an effective-date provision. It only says when the Act's amendments take effect, including a special rule for certain benefit years. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. The mention of 'benefit years' is about timing, not about any outside party taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: The amendments made by this Act shall take effect on January 1, 1972
opus.b: **Step 1: Reasoning.** There isn't a real temptation here. The word "benefit years" might suggest the benefits-application exclusion, but that exclusion doesn't come into play. The section only sets effective dates for amendments. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, no hearing or comment period is required, no rulemaking is authorized, and no right to sue is granted.

qwen_chat.w: This section solely establishes the effective dates for specific amendments to the Act. It does not create any process for consultation, coordination, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties. The mention of 'benefit years' refers to the temporal scope of the law's application, not to a participation mechanism or an application process.
qwen_chat.s: The amendments made by this Act shall take effect on January 1, 1972, except that the amendments made by sections 2(35) and 2(36) of this Act shall take effect only with respect to benefit years that begin on or after January 2, 1972.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section mentions "benefit years," it relates to benefits, and the definition excludes applications for benefits. However, this section does not describe an application process or a grant; it merely sets the effective date of the law. There is no mechanism for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. The text is purely procedural regarding the timing of the statute's enactment.
